punchline: Simon Sinek cites a study that S&P 500 companies once lasted about 61 years and now about 18, a sign that business has no final whistle.
thirty_sec: Soccer has fixed rules and a winner. Simon Sinek, borrowing from James Carse, says business isn't like that: players come and go, rules change, nobody wins for good. A finite-minded leader chases near-term profit and reacts to rivals. An infinite-minded one expects disruption and aims to come out stronger. He cites S&P 500 lifespans falling from about 61 years to about 18.
